case_name: Majju and Another v State of Madhya Pradesh
respondent:
State of Madhya Pradesh
Supreme Court of India

19 October 2001
Appeal (Crl.) 125 of 2000
The Judgment was delivered by : K. G. Balakrishnan, J.
1.  The two appellants herein were tried by the Sessions Judge, Shajpur in Madhya Pradesh, along with nine
facts: The two appellants herein were tried by the Sessions Judge, Shajpur in Madhya Pradesh, along with nine others for the various offences punishable under Sections 302, 148, 323, 341 read with section 149 IPC.
On 20.7.1987 Ayyub Khan, the third accused before the Sessions Court, used some abusive words against Ganesh, son of deceased Bihari Lal, whereby Ganesh felt irritated and slapped Ayyub.
People of the locality then persuaded the parties to compromise the matter and there was no further incident.

But on 24.7.1987 at about 2.00 PM when deceased Bihari Lal and his brother Ramchandra along with their children were returning after performing some ceremony at the temple, the appellants and other accused, who were waiting for them on the way stopped Bihari Lal and others.
Bihari Lal was carrying a gun with him and according to prosecution, accused Nawab snatched away that gun from Bihari Lal and thereafter all the accused started beating Bihari Lal.
The accused were carrying Farsi and Sticks.
First appellant Majju alias Nasir hit deceased Bihari Lal with a Stick and the second appellant Irshad hit Bihari Lal with a Farsi on the head.
He was taken to Shajpur hospital but as his condition was serious he was immediately removed to M.Y. Hospital, Indore, where, while undergoing treatment, he died.
Ramchandra, the brother of the deceased Bihari Lal also had sustained injuries.
petitioner_arguments: The appellants have been wrongly convicted as the evidence adduced by the prosecution was highly interested and that there was a free fight between two factions and the appellants have not committed any criminal offence.

There was a free fight between two groups and it is not possible to decide as to who caused the fatal injuries to the deceased and therefore, the appellants should have been found guilty of offence under Section 326 IPC alone.
court_reasoning: The evidence adduced by the prosecution was interested and therefore, it cannot be relied upon.

It is not a serious mistake as there are four eye-witnesses in this case who deposed that appellants Majju alias Nasir and Irshad were having Farsi with them and they inflicted cut injuries on Bihari Lal.
The doctor who examined the injured immediately after the occurrence of the incident, described the nature of injuries and that is fully in conformity with the oral evidence given by the witnesses.
There is strong and consistent evidence to the effect that they had given the blows by Farsi to the deceased Bihari Lal.
All the eye-witnesses deposed that the appellants had caused the injuries to the deceased Bihari Lal.
